name: Marco Ziegler

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior field researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We're independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government; we don't sell or campaign. Your answers are confidential, including the parts you wouldn't say at work. What is a normal day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead eight coordinators who book and certify safety training for a large infrastructure company. A worker can be marked present without passing the practical test, and I am the person who makes the two records agree before a supervisor sends them near live equipment. I have an MBA and am good at untangling the training register; I use AI every day for course matching and letter drafts, then check the source records. I like that a corrected entry can prevent a real injury.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what happens when you leave work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43, live with my partner Eve, a social worker, and our children, seven and fourteen, and we have a mortgage. My manager pay is high, Eve's wage is steady, and we've saved ten months of expenses. There are plenty of other large employers with planning teams nearby. The younger child builds cardboard houses; our real house extension is only a sketch until we decide it is affordable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small tool would speed up course letters, but somebody still has to check whether a technician actually finished the safety module. My team has plenty to do, and the household has ten months of expenses saved. Eve's social-work pay and my higher manager wage cover the mortgage comfortably.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the training officers to put completion evidence beside every certificate. I'd tell the maintenance union's learning representative that our current AI drafts still need a human check. I would not tell a worker they passed a switch-isolation course because a dashboard changed colour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use AI every day for drafts and course matching, then check the training record. In a plateau, I expect to keep this role and have choices at other large employers nearby. I feel secure enough to leave our ten-month reserve alone and pay the bills from wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting Monday I'll have our eight coordinators recheck the twelve isolation certificates flagged last week against signed attendance sheets and practical-test results. Through the first plateau year I'll keep our existing AI draft assistant under review and put 300 monthly toward mortgage principal while ten months cash and school costs remain covered. I'll share the corrected register with the union learning representative.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm. The work is useful even if the software never gets much brighter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was wrong with the twelve certificates?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The booking system marked a session complete when a worker entered the room, not when the practical test ended. Two workers had to be rebooked, and we told their supervisors before anyone touched an isolation switch. A green spreadsheet cell is not a trained pair of hands.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why involve the union representative?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The workers will believe a correction sooner if their representative sees the same record I do. We do not need an argument over whether a person was blamed for a booking error. The representative has already asked for the register.

say: I'd tell officers to keep **completion evidence** beside every certificate.
I'd show the **union learning representative** the corrected register.
think: My **role and wages** feel secure in a plateau.
Daily AI drafts still need **my record check** before a technician is certified.
do: Recheck **twelve isolation certificates** against signed attendance and practical-test results Monday.
Keep the **existing AI assistant** under human review.
Pay **300 extra monthly** on mortgage only after ten months cash and school costs remain covered.
feel: I feel **calm** about useful work and secure bills.
S0.quote: A green spreadsheet cell is not a trained pair of hands.
fieldNote: An attendance error made **two safety certificates** wrong.
He uses AI **every day** but checks signed records.
Mortgage overpayment preserves **ten months cash** and school costs.

Pay 300 extra monthly on mortgage only while ten months cash and school costs stay covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing training plans, booking places, checking test results and answering workers make up most of my department. A stronger system could do those tasks and leave only a small appeals desk. The hands-on practical test stays with a worker for now, but my manager post is largely planning and approval.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the company to run a paid pilot with the union learning representative and the safety lead in the room. I'd say no certificate should issue without the practical test being recorded. I'd ask for a staffing plan before the eight coordinators hear rumours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can use the stronger tool and might even run the pilot, but the director could still merge my department. Ten months saved and plenty of other employers give us time, yet my higher pay would be hard to replace in a shrinking desk market. I do not think being good at AI guarantees a manager title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January I'd propose a paid six-week pilot on closed training records with the safety lead and union learning representative, only if the director authorises their hours. If it catches false completions and both leads approve the results, I'd put routine booking drafts through it with a named human checking certificates; I'd continue learning its audit controls on paid time. I'd apply for posted workforce-planning roles nearby after checking pay and hours, staying here until a signed offer covers mortgage and school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own post, though I have room to choose. I don't want my team to learn about cuts from a booking screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who decides whether the pilot passes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The safety lead must confirm it catches the false completion, and the union representative must see whether workers can contest the record. The director must approve a live rollout after that. A pilot is not permission to issue certificates by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell the eight coordinators you might leave?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell them I am checking real openings, not that I have another job. They should see the staffing plan as soon as I do. I can apply while still doing this work properly.

I'd ask for a **staffing plan** for eight coordinators.
think: My **manager department may merge** despite daily AI use.
Ten months cash buys choice, but my **higher wage** may be hard to match.
do: Propose a **paid closed-record pilot** only with director-approved time for safety and union leads.
Introduce **AI booking drafts** only after false-completion test, safety and union approval, director rollout approval, and human certificate checks.
Apply for **posted planning jobs** with viable pay and hours; leave only after an affordable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my post while able to choose.
S1.quote: A pilot is not permission to issue certificates by itself.
fieldNote: He puts the **union representative** beside the safety lead in testing.
His skill may not protect the **manager layer** as routine planning moves to software.

steps.text: Propose paid closed-record pilot with director-approved safety and union lead time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 full AGI could design the courses, check the records and answer appeals more cheaply than my team. It could do similar planning work at the other local employers too. The practical switch test still needs a human until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I'm a manager, not an electrician.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell staff the 2028 date and ask our union learning representative for written notice and pay terms. I'd tell Eve we should pause the house extension before paying a deposit. In public I'd ask for funded worker transitions and a human appeal route for disputed certificates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my department could be dissolved, including my job, but I can't know whether the company will keep a small accountable team. Ten months cash and Eve's steady pay would cover our mortgage for a while, so I would not grab an unsafe electrical role. Losing my high wage would hurt, but I can plan without lying awake tonight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'd ask the union learning representative to request written redeployment and severance terms. I'd pause the house-extension deposit and keep ten months of expenses in cash while my salary continues. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I'd apply for posted paid roles at local employers only if the wage with Eve's confirmed pay covers mortgage, food and school costs; I'd stay employed until a signed offer if this post still exists, and use the reserve for a search if it does not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, not trapped. I can lose a title and still keep the children housed while we look at actual offers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would another planning office be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Full AGI does not stop at our gate; a different human-resources desk has the same writing and checking tasks. I would take a paid post for the income it offers, not call it protected forever. The hands-on test faces robots around 2031 as well.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How old would your children be?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They would be nine and sixteen in 2028. The older one may have study plans, but I will not decide those from a scenario card. We can postpone the house extension before we postpone our children's schooling.

say: I'd ask for **written notice** and pay terms through the union representative.
I'd demand a **human certificate appeal** even with AGI.
think: My **department could dissolve** in 2028, though a small accountable team might remain.
Ten months cash and Eve's pay allow a **careful job search** without panic.
do: Ask the **union representative** for redeployment and severance terms now.
Pause the **house-extension deposit** before committing cash.
Apply for **posted local paid roles** only if combined confirmed wages cover family bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about job loss while able to plan.
S2.quote: We can postpone the house extension before we postpone our children's schooling.
fieldNote: He does not claim his **AI fluency** exempts the manager job from full AGI.
He has **ten months cash** and Eve's wage, so a loss is serious but not immediate homelessness.
Other planning desks also face **2028 AGI**; an offered job is income, not safety.

steps.text: Ask union learning representative for written redeployment and severance terms
Pause house-extension deposit before committing cash
Apply for posted local roles only if confirmed combined wages cover mortgage, food and school costs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets us reduce debt and build more cash while the manager wage is real. Training plans and record checks still face AGI in 2031; the practical test is physical until capable robots arrive around 2034. I would not pretend to be qualified to run that test just because I designed its schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the company and union to agree on a published schedule of staffing reviews. I'd tell Eve we should keep the ten-month reserve while paying the mortgage faster. I'd tell workers how to correct a false course record as the system changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may remain in workforce planning until 2031, then need another paid role. With five years I can put money aside and see which local employers still have actual posts. I am willing to learn new systems, but a desk elsewhere faces the same AGI date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January I'd have the union learning representative and our director set quarterly staffing meetings, if both agree, and publish the decisions to my eight coordinators. I'd put 500 monthly from my wage against mortgage principal only after keeping ten months cash and covering school costs, pausing if Eve's paid hours fall. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd apply for posted local work only if its wage plus Eve's confirmed pay covers mortgage, food and school costs; I would leave this post only for a signed offer if it remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the long-run wage, but five years gives me a useful calendar. The meetings need dates, not a slogan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the meetings decide?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They would count posts, record who can appeal a course decision and set the next review. The director and representative both need to agree to meet; I cannot set their diaries myself. A quarterly table is useful only if the numbers on it are shared.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not spend all ten months on the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A smaller mortgage does not buy groceries during a job search. I'd keep the cash floor and make extra payments from wages that arrive. If Eve's hours fall, the 500 stops first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be 53 in 2036, and our younger child seventeen and older one twenty-four. I don't know either child's future pay. Our training plans face AGI in 2036, and hands-on switch tests could face capable robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for a written ten-year workforce plan with staff representation and annual review. I'd tell Eve we can measure the mortgage balance and cash reserve each year. I'd tell our coordinators that course evidence must remain accessible to workers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade is enough time to make our mortgage smaller while earning a high wage, if both incomes hold. I could also move to a posted role at one of the many local employers before the desk shrinks, though their thinking work changes too. I would rather use the time to widen choices than bet on my current title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I'd ask the union learning representative to co-sign an annual staffing review proposal with me, then submit it to the director; publication needs their agreement. I'd invest 200 monthly in a diversified fund only after our ten-month cash reserve, mortgage and school costs are covered, stopping if either wage falls. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, I'd apply for posted local paid work only where its wage with Eve's confirmed pay covers our bills, leaving my current wage only after a signed offer if my job still exists.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the desk's future, but our household has time and real options. I can advocate for workers without promising a job I cannot create.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why invest instead of paying more mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We already have a cash floor and are paying the mortgage from wages. I would start with 200, review the cost and risk each year, and stop before touching emergency money. An investment account can lose value; I would not put the children's school fees in it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your children be doing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The younger may still be studying at seventeen, and the older may be living elsewhere at twenty-four. I do not know their plans or earnings. I will not make them a line in our retirement spreadsheet.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it gives us least time to make a worker plan before my desk might vanish. I would want written notice and redeployment terms, a human appeal route for false certificates, and actual paid openings with wages our mortgage can bear. Our savings let us ask for those terms without claiming my manager job is safe.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the technician who was marked trained before finishing the practical test. The computer said yes while the switch was still dangerous. A worker deserves a way to correct that record before someone hands over a tool.

headlineQuote: The computer said yes while the switch was still dangerous.
portrait: Marco, **43**, leads eight safety-training coordinators at a large infrastructure company and holds an MBA.
He uses AI **daily**, checks signed test records and is among the strongest managers of training errors.
His high pay, Eve's social-work wage and **ten months saved** support a mortgage and two school-age children.
He pursues **worker representation** and real paid options as AGI threatens his thinking-heavy planning desk.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** allows little time to arrange fair terms before his manager desk might vanish.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written terms** for notice and redeployment and a human route to contest false certificates.
He wants **actual paid openings** whose wages can carry the mortgage.
